objective: Prepare ordered module namespace import candidates once per export-syntax summary instead of repeatedly parsing every path/target pair.
limitations: One matched four-module diagnostic pair. The full-build baseline is the preceding semantic-name-index iteration measurement; the new candidate uses the exact same frozen workspace path, source digests, dependency sources, native toolchain, dev profile and eight jobs. This is not a statistical performance or CI guarantee.

Each cold build starts with an empty target and private compiled-artifact cache; dependency sources and OS page cache are retained. No compiler builds, tests or external profiler overlap the timed full builds or measured diagnostic pair.

Diagnostic executables use matching extra operation counters and Clang 23 -O3. Counters reset after workspace loading; one-time candidate preparation is included in lowering_ms, while serialization and output hashing are excluded. Nested operation durations must not be summed.

Candidate preparation preserves source-path and target order, uses the original alias resolver, and falls back to the original complete target scan for incomplete/editor syntax. Existing positive/negative query caching is unchanged. There are no persistent cache-format or runtime C changes.
Native tests run on Linux x86_64 with Clang 23.1.3; fresh extreme bootstrap stages use Ubuntu 24.04 / Clang 18 Docker. Other native OS CI platforms have not run.
